scope: Capability-first Go tooling design from a complete410-current-source discovery pass. User explicitly rejects migrating every historical script. This is a design and evidence map, not implemented tooling or retirement approval.

static_cross_file_candidates.meaning: Ranked static review leads, including whole functions and nonoverlapping blocks; not semantic equivalence or projected savings.

toolkit_interface: Keep one Go program with a small set of operation families; share existing parsers/codecs/planner/writer. CLI operations need not become separate binaries, packages or handlers per historical script.

capabilities.name: text and consumer layout
capabilities.shared_engine: Decode/encode source grammar, load native font/space metrics, measure text and bounded substitutions, apply permitted word/line/page layout, report overflow. Reuse encode, controls, wrapPages and inspect.
capabilities.data: Canonical English by registry ID; proven box/callsite profile; width, row/page policy, chosen scale, expansion domain, copy/stride bounds and explicit exceptional controls.
capabilities.remaining_gap: Independent authoring preview; measured-width wrapping; scale and positioned/substituted geometry. Current character-budget wrapping and target-pinned replay are not a complete authoring tool.

capabilities.name: guarded binary and image patching
capabilities.shared_engine: Plan guarded byte/word edits, validate ranges/overlap, allocate capacity, update typed references, create exclusive copies and verify readback. Reuse plan, inspect, validateEdits, verifySource, patchCopy, isoFileExtent and existing word templates/fixups.
capabilities.data: Old/new words, stable IDs, pointer sites, source stages, approved reservations, hook templates and ABI/precondition evidence.
capabilities.remaining_gap: Consumer ABI, signed-high/low pairs, shared-LUI liveness, copy bounds and cave/landing safety remain distinct proof obligations, not generic address search.

capabilities.name: asset authoring and packaging
capabilities.shared_engine: PS2 texture/index/palette codecs, bounded raster/font rendering or reconstruction, named CMB/ISO replacement through existing planBundle and writer.
capabilities.data: Sheet/spec masks, font choices, label content, palette/alpha rules, target member names and source/target hashes.
capabilities.remaining_gap: Current Go covers pinned replacement transport, not all semantic texture/raster authoring.

capabilities.name: registry import and reconciliation
capabilities.shared_engine: Resolve canonical IDs, import/merge fields under explicit human/machine ownership, detect conflicts, reconcile installed bytes and record guarded metadata updates.
capabilities.data: English, glossary, explicit canonical-ID repairs, batch selectors and provenance.
capabilities.remaining_gap: Port only current needed behavior. Dated repair batches are provenance/data, not separate reusable commands.

capabilities.name: offline inspection and verification
capabilities.shared_engine: Reuse format and reference parsers to inspect, compare source/target bytes, measure layout, audit typed references and produce evidence/diffs.
capabilities.data: Selectors, expected states, comparison semantics and review reports.
capabilities.remaining_gap: A heuristic xref or markup-stripped display comparison cannot prove exact semantic controls, liveness or physical fit.

capabilities.name: owned runtime probing
capabilities.shared_engine: Owned session lifecycle, PINE reads/input, capture and typed scenario comparison. Reuse existing ownership-aware implementations rather than copying global teardown.
capabilities.data: Scenario steps, addresses, expected values, screenshots and fault conditions.
capabilities.remaining_gap: Optional supporting domain until needed for active authoring validation.39 source paths contain app-wide kill commands; retain PID/starttime/ISO ownership instead.

engine_vs_data_rules: A wording, address, texture name, approved scale or box-specific limit is data when the same algorithm and ownership contract apply.
Independent codecs, consumer line/copy semantics, ABI/liveness analysis, source identity and output ownership remain explicit responsibilities.
Tests preserve important contracts; one old test file or diagnostic output format is not a new tool requirement.
No new function when an existing function can reasonably own the behavior. Document reuse/callers before an unavoidable new boundary; fewer function names alone do not establish readability.
Generate encoded target hashes/measurements as evidence rather than requiring authors to hand-maintain duplicated derived facts. Do not weaken strict apply checks for authoring.

first_implementation.task: Prove a small independent read-only text-fitting preview using existing native metrics and codec functions before choosing its final CLI/schema seam.
must_work_without: complete pointer set or free allocation space
outputs: Actual encoded bytes/hash and byte count
Measured native widths and line/page information
Selected profile/scale and unresolved substitutions or geometry
first_implementation.safety: No writable edits or apply path from preview. Source/font/profile identity and control semantics remain checked; strict plan/verifySource/patchCopy stay unchanged.
scope_sequence: Synthetic proof for one known plain consumer, with changed English and source preservation.
Measured wrapping and profile rules across paged dialogue versus no-PAGE descriptions.
Scale/center/nested substitution support only after the corresponding measurement/consumer contract is proven.
first_implementation.acceptance: Demonstrate recurring use cases through the same shared implementation and purpose-grouped profile/recipe data; then remove actually superseded implementations after caller/behavior review. Do not resume one-script-at-a-time migration.

limits: All410 current bodies were statically crawled; dynamic callbacks and runtime consumer behavior are not exhaustively proved.
Historical bodies with mismatching pins are capability references, not exact byte oracles.
Six capability areas are a design map, not a claim all six are implemented or each requires a new tool.
No ISO writes, registry updates, emulator/PINE use, new gameplay proof or deletion authorization in this pass.

latest_user_direction.goal: A reasonable, human-readable reusable toolkit for all14 core responsibilities; enhance each existing owner later as more cases arise. Exhaustive historical-script or workflow-family coverage is not a prerequisite for a usable toolset.
latest_user_direction.verification: Focused changed-behavior tests during development; full integrated/race suite towards the end. Preserve source/write safety.
acceptance: A meaningful ordinary workflow and explicit inputs/outputs for each core responsibility.
Existing owner and clear data-versus-behavior extension path; no14 separate handlers or speculative interfaces.
Explicit unsupported cases fail clearly; no claim that breadth implies full coverage.
Integrated workflow verification before final toolkit completion.
latest_user_direction.next: Use the verified14-area baseline and existing-owner map for future concrete mod cases. Enhance data/owners where behavior requires it; do not recreate historical CLIs or chase exhaustive coverage.

integrated_baseline.limits: Availability, not100% reuse/full-family/historical completion. Existing legacy gaps and historical references remain recorded.
